title: Spin a RealSense camera onto a loose ball head's 1/4"-20 stud, stop it facing the work area, lock it with the wheel
instruction: Mount the camera so it faces the robot's workspace.
context: Robot data-collection rigs need fixed third-person cameras; fitting a RealSense to an arm's ball head is routine rig setup. The head's pan base is loose, so turning the camera turns the head unless the other hand holds it, and the camera must stop facing the tape before the wheel locks it.
setup: A desk (the table) in front of two arms whose bases are 61 cm apart; distances are forward from the line between the bases and sideways from their midpoint (right negative). (1) An articulating camera arm (black aluminium, two 20 mm tubes with ball knuckles), its super clamp on the desk's far edge 91 cm forward on a line 16 cm right, reaching in to a ball head. (2) The ball head, fixed on the arm: a 40 mm panning base (loose: everything above it swivels freely about the vertical), a 32 mm aluminium socket body 33 mm tall with its ball locked upright by its knob, a 35 mm platform with a rubber pad, its top face 10 cm above the desk, centred 40 cm forward and 16 cm right. On the platform a steel 1/4"-20 UNC stud stands 10 mm tall, and a black knurled steel lock wheel (1/4"-20, 40 mm across, 4 mm thick, 10 g) is run down onto the platform. A white line on the socket body and one on the pan base mark the head's start. (3) A 12 mm blue tape strip on the desk from under the stud 15 cm straight towards the arms, with an arrowhead: the forward line. (4) An Intel RealSense D435 depth camera, loose: an aluminium bar 90 x 25 x 25 mm, 75 g, glass front with four lens windows, a 1/4"-20 tripod hole in the middle of its underside. It stands on its underside centred 23 cm forward and 18 cm right, its long side across the arms' forward axis, lenses facing away from the arms. Distractors, not scored: (5) a ceramic mug (11.4 x 9 x 8 cm, 300 g) at 42 cm forward, 24 cm left; (6) a roll of clear tape (10 cm across, 5 cm tall, 60 g) at 56 cm forward, 5 cm left; (7) a Phillips No. 2 screwdriver (19 cm long, 100 g) at 56 cm forward, 33 cm right. The layout is the same every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end state, read at every control step. Caught: the camera is threaded on the stud (in simulation, the thread catches when the camera, resting on the stud's first thread with its hole within 0.6 mm of the stud's axis and tilted under 5 degrees, is turned clockwise past where the thread starts meet; turned back past that point it comes off). Gap: the camera base's height above the platform minus the lock wheel's 4.0 mm. Aim: the angle between the camera's lens axis and the tape, seen from above. Head moved: the head's turn on its pan base from the start (the two marks). Wheel gap: between the wheel's top and the camera's base. Hands clear: every fingertip at least 3 cm from the camera and from the head above its base. 0.0 if the camera has ever been dropped (fell faster than 0.8 m/s), whatever happens later. 1.0: caught, gap at most 1.0 mm, aim within 5 degrees, head moved no more than 5 degrees, wheel gap at most 0.3 mm, hands clear, everything still, held for 1 s. 0.75: caught, gap at most 1.0 mm and aim within 5 degrees, without the rest of 1.0. 0.5: caught and gap at most 1.0 mm, aim more than 5 degrees off. 0.25: caught, gap more than 1.0 mm (on but loose). 0.0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Full credit lapses as soon as its state does.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Unscrew the camera, run the lock wheel down to the platform, turn the head's pan mark back to its tape mark, and stand the camera on its marks.
fidelity: Isaac Sim PhysX, 20 Hz. The thread is not geometry: a D6 joint switched on at the catch keeps the camera on the stud's axis, adds 0.02 N m s/rad drag (pan base 0.002) and draws it 1.27 mm a turn. The wheel's rise follows its turn in code (8 N cap); run hard against the camera it is held from turning, as a jam nut is. Camera, head, arm and wheel are primitives at real size; no USB cable. Uniform friction; no force sensing.
